If you've shipped prod for 15 years, you assume 90% of AI devtools are toys. Aura stands up to real engineering scrutiny.

{[ { q: '"Does Aura replace Git?"', a: "No. Aura is a meta-layer that sits directly on top of your existing local Git repository. You keep your normal Git workflow (`git commit`, `git push`, branch management). Aura acts as a parasitic engine that tracks the mathematical logic (AST) inside those files, giving you AI-specific superpowers without forcing you to abandon the tools you already know." }, { q: '"Why not just have developers commit more often instead of tracking every save?"', a: "Because AI operates non-linearly. A human types linearly and commits. An AI can refactor a schema, update three routes, and change frontend state in 14 seconds across 8 files. A developer literally cannot run `git commit` fast enough to isolate those logic decisions. Aura provides the Continuous DVR so when the AI hallucinates at minute 12, you don't lose the good code from minute 1." }, { q: '"Why do I need a vector database? Why not just write better PR descriptions?"', a: "PR descriptions are static snapshots of the final state. They do not capture the AI's internal reasoning. If an AI adds obscure exponential backoff, the PR just says 'Added retry logic.' Months later, you don't know if it was a hallucination or if the AI read a rate-limit doc.
